title: Fungi UI theming: decisions before the spike

questions.prompt: Which direction should lead the 2nd theme?
questions.context:
Switch tabs in the preview to compare the same outcome page in each direction; region comments work on any tab. These are rough sketches, not the real kit.

I checked all 10 linked sites in a browser: 8 of the 11 references are light, reading-first article pages. Their palettes are warm off-white or near-white; their type is serif or monospace; they separate content with thin rules instead of boxed cards.

| Direction | Drawn from | Character |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A · Paper | hugo.blog, Distill, Wikipedia, the arXiv page, Low-tech Magazine, sonnet.io | Serif reading column, ruled tables and rows, ink-black actions |
| B · Mono | interfaces.dev image, growingSWE, Palais de Tokyo | All monospace, hairline boxes, dashed dividers, uppercase labels |
| C · Neutral | shadcn, ciechanow.ski, MLU Explain | System sans, zinc greys, rounded cards with soft shadows |

Unless you veto one in Notes, I plan to build all three as real theme files so you can switch between them in the gallery. Your pick gets the most polish and becomes the candidate.
questions.recommendation: A · Paper. Outcome is mostly reading, and the references cluster here. It is also the clearest break from the current "bootstrap" feel. C risks reading as a generic component library again, and B makes long prose tiring to read.

options.label: A · Paper (editorial)
B · Mono (technical)
C · Neutral (component library)

questions.prompt: How should the 2nd theme relate to light and dark?
questions.context: The current theme is dark-only, and every template sets `color-scheme: dark`. A theme sets `color-scheme` itself, so native checkboxes and scrollbars follow it.
questions.recommendation: Light-only 2nd theme. It gives the clearest contrast to the dark baseline and the smallest spike. The token names stay mode-neutral, so a dark variant can be added later without renaming anything.

options.label: 2nd theme is light-only; current theme stays dark
Every theme ships light and dark, following the OS setting
2nd theme is also dark: a restyle within dark

questions.prompt: Who decides which theme a window uses?
questions.context:
The accepted authoring boundary says routine callers never choose UI. So a theme must be either fixed by the workflow or applied mechanically, never chosen by the agent each round.

Mechanism I plan to use in every case: `data-theme="name"` on `<html>` plus one `themes/name.css` file. Its tokens use zero specificity, so a workflow's own CSS still wins.
questions.recommendation: Workflow default plus a personal preference. Each workflow keeps a default, and a small user-level setting read by the shared assembler can override it. Agents never pick; you set it once.

options.label: Workflow default, overridable by a personal setting the assembler reads
Each workflow pins its theme in its template; nothing else
A switcher inside the window (persistence across sessions unverified)
The agent picks per round through the input JSON

questions.prompt: How far may a theme go beyond colours and type?
questions.context:
| Reach | Theme can change | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tokens only | Colours, fonts, sizes, radii, spacing, borders, shadows | Paper gets serif text but keeps boxed choices |
| Tokens + scoped rules | The above, plus per-component CSS inside the theme file | Paper draws choices as ruled rows and tables in booktabs style |

Scoped rules use `:where([data-theme=…])`, so they never outrank a workflow's overrides. Component markup and JS are identical in both cases.
questions.recommendation: Tokens + scoped rules. Paper and Mono both depend on structural differences (rules instead of boxes, booktabs tables). Tokens alone would give a recoloured version of the current look.

options.label: Tokens plus scoped structural rules
Tokens only

questions.prompt: Can themes bundle font files, or system fonts only?
questions.context:
Pages are offline, and their CSP blocks network fonts. `outcome.html` allows no font source; grill-form allows only `data:` fonts. On macOS, system stacks give New York / Iowan Old Style / Charter for serif and SF Mono for monospace. Windows and Linux fall back to Georgia / Consolas or similar.

Bundling would mean vendoring OFL fonts with their licences (e.g. Source Serif 4, IBM Plex Mono) and adding `font-src 'self'` to each template. That adds roughly 100–300 KB per assembled bundle.
questions.recommendation: System fonts only for this spike. The candidates already look right on macOS with Iowan and SF Mono. Revisit bundling once a direction is picked, if it depends on a specific face.

options.label: System font stacks only (for now)
Bundle one or two open-licence fonts

questions.prompt: What happens to the current dark theme?
questions.context: The token refactor rewrites every colour in `ui.css` as a variable. Keeping the current look pixel-identical lets a screenshot comparison prove the refactor broke nothing.
questions.recommendation: Freeze it pixel-identical as the baseline ("classic"), and keep it the default until you choose otherwise. Refreshing it is a separate, later step.

options.label: Freeze it pixel-identical; keep it the default
Refresh it in this spike too, using the chosen direction
Retire it once the 2nd theme lands

questions.prompt: Should themes reach inside sandboxed previews?
questions.context: Interactive previews (prototypes, visual options) are authored HTML in an isolated frame with its own styles. Today they ignore the page theme.
questions.recommendation: Leave previews as authored. A preview shows the design being judged, and theming it would change what is under review. If a need appears later, tokens can be offered as opt-in variables.

options.label: Leave previews as authored
Offer theme tokens inside previews as opt-in CSS variables
Apply the window theme to previews by default

questions.prompt: Anything that would make you reject a theme, or that it must have?
questions.context: For example: what makes something feel "too much" the way ShowAI does, a contrast or size floor, or how dense it should be.
